88013826.extract:
# Multo (song)

"**Multo**" (transl. "Ghost") is a song recorded by the Filipino pop band Cup of Joe for their debut studio album, *Silakbo* (2025). It was written by the band's co-lead vocalist Raphaell Ridao and his brother Redentor Immanuel Ridao, with production handled by Shadiel Chan and Jovel Rivera. Viva Records released the song as the album's lead single on September 14, 2024. A synth-pop and pop-rock ballad, "Multo" lyrically utilizes the metaphor of a ghost to describe the lingering presence of a past lover and the inescapable nature of grief.

The song achieved significant commercial success both domestically and internationally. "Multo" became the first song by a Filipino act to enter the *Billboard* Global 200 chart, where it peaked at number 80. In the Philippines, the single topped the *Billboard* Philippines Hot 100 for 27 consecutive weeks, establishing the record for the longest-running number-one song in the chart's history. It was recognized as the most-streamed local song of 2025 by Spotify Philippines and the top OPM song of the year by Apple Music Philippines.

An accompanying music video, directed by Kris Cazin, was released in March 2025. The video features actors Elijah Canlas and Miles Ocampo in a narrative depicting a relationship haunted by memories. The song received critical praise for its emotional depth and was cited as a turning point in the band's artistic maturity. It won Song of the Year at the 2025 Filipino Music Awards.

## Background and release

Cup of Joe, a band based in Baguio, Philippines, formed in 2018 and gained initial popularity with songs such as "Tingin" and "Estranghero" . During the COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns in 2020, lead vocalist Raphaell Ridao and his brother, Redentor Immanuel Ridao, wrote "Multo" while confined in their home . According to Raphaell, the isolation of the pandemic provided time for reflection, and the songwriting process served as an outlet for emotions regarding loss and the feeling of being "haunted" by unexplainable thoughts .

The band announced the single's release only three hours prior to its launch . "Multo" was officially released on digital platforms on September 14, 2024, under Viva Records . It served as the lead single for the band's debut studio album, *Silakbo* (transl. "Outburst"), which was subsequently released on January 17, 2025 . The track is situated as the seventh song on the album, which is conceptually structured around the five stages of grief; "Multo" represents the stage of depression .

## Composition and lyrics

"Multo" is a synth-pop and pop-rock ballad with a duration of three minutes and fifty-seven seconds . The song was produced by Shadiel Chan and Jovel Rivera, with arrangements by the Ridao brothers, Chan, and the band .

Lyrically, the song explores themes of grief, heartbreak, and emotional haunting . The title "Multo" refers to a "ghost" or figure that follows a person, symbolizing memories or feelings that persist despite attempts to move on . Raphaell Ridao stated that the song was conceived from the idea of feelings that follow someone regardless of their efforts to push them away .

The lyrics depict a protagonist who is unable to escape the memory of a past love, with lines such as "Pasindi na ng ilaw / Minumulto na 'ko ng damdamin ko" (transl. "Turn on the lights / I am being haunted by my feelings") . Critics have noted that while the song addresses romantic loss, the "ghost" imagery has been interpreted by listeners as applying to various forms of loss, including the death of loved ones, faded friendships, or past versions of oneself .

## Critical reception

Music critics responded favorably to "Multo," often highlighting it as a sign of Cup of Joe's musical evolution. *Rolling Stone Philippines* described the track as a "synth-pop ballad" that revealed an "emotional depth fans hadn't anticipated" from a band previously known for upbeat pop tracks . The review noted that the song marked the band's arrival as "serious pop storytellers" and described the track as a "slow-burning phenomenon" that grew in popularity well after its initial release .

The song's production and lyrical content were praised for their maturity. *Billboard Philippines* noted that the track solidified the band's impact on the Philippine soundscape . The song's ability to resonate with a broad audience was attributed to its open-ended interpretability regarding grief and loss .

## Commercial performance

"Multo" achieved historic chart performance for a Filipino artist. In April 2025, the song debuted at number 181 on the *Billboard* Global 200, making Cup of Joe the first Filipino act to enter the chart . The song eventually peaked at number 80 on the Global 200 . Additionally, it debuted at number 74 on the *Billboard* Global Excl. U.S. chart, marking the highest debut for a Filipino song on that chart and the first to enter the top 100; it later peaked at number 33 .

In the Philippines, "Multo" was a dominant commercial force throughout 2025. It topped the *Billboard* Philippines Hot 100 for 27 consecutive weeks, setting a record for the longest-running number-one song in the chart's history . It surpassed the previous record held by Dionela's "Marilag" . The song also led the Top Philippine Songs chart for the same duration .

On streaming platforms, "Multo" was the most-streamed local song of 2025 on Spotify Philippines . It reportedly broke records for the most single-day streams for a Filipino song on Spotify, reaching approximately 2.3 million plays in a 24-hour period . Apple Music Philippines also ranked "Multo" as the number one song on its "Top OPM Songs of 2025" list .

## Music video

The official music video for "Multo" was released on March 6, 2025 . It was directed by Kris Cazin and stars actors Elijah Canlas and Miles Ocampo . The casting of Canlas and Ocampo, who were a former couple in real life, was noted by media outlets as adding a layer of emotional authenticity to the video's narrative of lost love .

The video's screenplay, written by the band, depicts a narrative where Ocampo's character experiences hallucinations of her partner, played by Canlas . The visual storytelling alternates between scenes of happy memories shared by the couple in a home and shots of Ocampo alone, implying that Canlas's character is a "ghost" or a memory she is struggling to release . The video was produced by Viva Records and has garnered millions of views on YouTube .

Picture this: a six-piece band from Baguio, Philippines, strumming their way out of cozy coffee shops and into the global spotlight with a song about a ghost. No, this isn’t the plot of a quirky indie film—it’s the real-life story of Cup of Joe and their viral sensation “Multo,” a track that’s not only possessed the hearts of Filipino fans but also spooked its way onto the Billboard Global 200, Billboard Global Excl. US, and Spotify Global charts. With a blend of catchy melodies, heartbreak vibes, and a music video starring Elijah Canlas and Miles Ocampo, “Multo” is the underdog anthem that’s rewriting the rules for OPM (Original Pilipino Music) on the world stage. So, grab a cup of joe (sorry, had to), and let’s dive into the phenomenon that’s got everyone haunted.

From Baguio to Billboard: The Rise of Cup of Joe
------------------------------------------------

Cup of Joe isn’t your typical boy band churning out cookie-cutter pop. Formed in 2019, this Baguio-based sextet—Raphael Ridao (vocals), Gabriel Fernandez (guitar), CJ Fernandez (guitar), Gian Bernardino (keys), Xen Gareza (bass), and Ralph Gavieres (drums)—started as a group of college buddies jamming for fun. Their sound? Think alternative pop with a side of nostalgia, blending introspective lyrics with earworm hooks that make you want to sway and sob simultaneously. Songs like “Misteryoso,” “Tingin,” and “Estranghero” built them a loyal local following, but it was “Multo,” released on September 14, 2024, as the lead single from their debut album Silakbo, that catapulted them into uncharted territory.

The band’s name, inspired by a casual coffee reference, reflects their laid-back vibe, but don’t let that fool you—these guys are brewing something serious. Hailing from Baguio, a city known for its cool climate and artistic soul, Cup of Joe channels that creative energy into music that feels both intimate and universal. As one X user put it, “Who would’ve thought a Baguio-based band would make it this far?” Well, apparently, the universe did.

“Multo”: A Ghost Story That’s Anything But Dead
-----------------------------------------------

At its core, “Multo” is a breakup song dressed in supernatural metaphors. The title, meaning “ghost” in Filipino, refers to the lingering presence of a past love—those memories that haunt you long after the relationship’s gone cold. With lyrics that hit like a bittersweet punch and a melody that sticks like superglue, it’s no wonder the song resonated with listeners. The track’s production, polished yet raw, captures the band’s signature sound: think Ben&Ben meets The 1975, with a distinctly Pinoy flair.

But what turned “Multo” from a local gem into a global juggernaut? Timing, talent, and a sprinkle of viral magic. Released as part of Silakbo (meaning “outburst” or “flare-up” in Filipino), the song dropped just as social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram were craving fresh, emotional anthems. Fans began sharing snippets, pairing the song’s heartfelt chorus with everything from dramatic breakup montages to aesthetic coffee shop reels. Before long, “Multo” was racking up streams—over 60 million on Spotify alone, [according to GMA News](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942862/cup-of-joe-multo-billboard-global-200/story/)—and climbing charts faster than you can say “OPM supremacy.”

The music video, released in March 2025, added fuel to the fire. Starring Elijah Canlas and Miles Ocampo, two of the Philippines’ brightest young actors, the video weaves a cinematic tale of love and loss that amplifies the song’s emotional heft. Directed with a keen eye for storytelling, it’s the kind of visual that makes you hit replay before the credits roll. [As GMA News reported](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/938503/cup-of-joe-drops-multo-music-video-starring-elijah-canlas-and-miles-ocampo/story/), the video’s star power and narrative depth helped cement “Multo” as a cultural moment.

Charting New Territory: A Filipino First
----------------------------------------

Let’s talk numbers, because “Multo” didn’t just make waves—it caused a tsunami. On April 15, 2025, [Billboard Philippines](https://billboardphilippines.com/market/chart-beat/cup-of-joe-are-the-first-filipino-act-to-break-into-the-billboard-global-200/) announced that the song had debuted at No. 181 on the Billboard Global 200, making Cup of Joe the first Filipino act ever to crack this prestigious chart. Not content with one historic flex, “Multo” also landed at No. 74 on the Billboard Global Excl. US chart—the highest debut for a Filipino song and the first to break into the Top 100. For context, it outranked tracks by global heavyweights like Jennie and Dua Lipa’s “Handlebars” (No. 186) and Rosé’s “Toxic Til The End” (No. 190) that week. No offense to K-pop queens, but that’s the kind of slay that deserves a mic drop.

Spotify’s Global charts tell a similar story of domination. “Multo” first entered the daily Global Top 200 at No. 164, but its climb was relentless. By April 7, it had surged 91 spots to No. 73 with 1.631 million streams, earning the title of “greatest gainer”. A few days later, it peaked at No. 28 with 2.557 million streams, breaking the record for the biggest single-day streams for a Filipino song. By April 19, it had jumped to No. 30 on the weekly Global Spotify chart with a staggering 17.582 million streams—the most weekly streams for any Filipino song in history and the first to crack the Top 50. It later re-peaked at No. 24 with 2.346 million streams. In a world dominated by Western pop and Latin bangers, a Filipino song holding its own is nothing short of revolutionary.

Why “Multo” Matters: A Win for OPM
----------------------------------

To understand the weight of “Multo”’s success, you need to zoom out. The Billboard Global 200 and Global Excl. US charts, launched in 2020, track streaming and sales data from over 200 territories. They’re the gold standard for measuring global music consumption, and breaking in is like getting a seat at the cool kids’ table—except the table’s guarded by Beyoncé and Bad Bunny. Before “Multo,” the only Filipino song to even graze the Global Excl. US chart was [Juan Karlos’ “ERE,” which debuted at No. 138](https://billboardphilippines.com/market/chart-beat/cup-of-joe-are-the-first-filipino-act-to-break-into-the-billboard-global-200/) in October 2023. For Cup of Joe to not only enter but dominate these charts is a game-changer for OPM.

The Philippines has a rich musical heritage, but OPM has often struggled to penetrate global markets dominated by Western acts. Multo’s success signals a shift—a crack in the glass ceiling that’s kept Filipino artists on the sidelines. As [Billboard Philippines](https://billboardphilippines.com/market/chart-beat/cup-of-joe-are-the-first-filipino-act-to-break-into-the-billboard-global-200/) noted, the song’s chart performance “showcases the alternative group’s rising impact on both the local and global stages”. It’s not just about one band; it’s about proving that Filipino stories, sung in Filipino, can resonate universally. When an X user wrote, “Goosebumps!” about the debut, they weren’t just hyping the song—they were celebrating a cultural milestone.

The Secret Sauce: What Makes “Multo” Click?
-------------------------------------------

So, what’s the alchemy behind “Multo”’s global takeover? First, there’s the song itself: a masterclass in balancing accessibility with authenticity. Its melody is instantly hummable, but the lyrics—rooted in Filipino experiences of love and loss—give it depth. It’s the kind of track that feels personal yet universal, like a diary entry you didn’t know you wrote.

Second, there’s the power of the internet. Streaming platforms like Spotify and social media have leveled the playing field, letting a band from Baguio compete with global superstars. “Multo”’s TikTok virality wasn’t an accident—it was a testament to how fans can amplify a song’s reach. Third, Cup of Joe’s underdog charm helps. They’re not a manufactured pop machine; they’re real people making music that feels honest. In a world of autotune and algorithms, that authenticity is catnip for listeners.

Finally, there’s the cultural moment. Filipino pop culture is having a renaissance, from films like Rewind breaking box office records to artists like SB19 topping charts. “Multo” rode that wave, proving that OPM isn’t just for karaoke nights—it’s for the world stage.

What’s Next for Cup of Joe?
---------------------------

With Silakbo out in the wild and “Multo” still haunting charts, Cup of Joe is at a crossroads. Will they lean into their global appeal with English-language tracks, or double down on Filipino storytelling? Either way, they’ve got the world’s attention. Their next moves—new singles, international tours, maybe a collab with a global act—could solidify their place as OPM’s new torchbearers.

For now, the band seems content to soak in the moment. As they told [Billboard Philippines](https://billboardphilippines.com/market/chart-beat/cup-of-joe-are-the-first-filipino-act-to-break-into-the-billboard-global-200/), “Multo” is about “capturing the essence of lingering emotions,” and that’s exactly what they’ve done—not just for fans, but for an entire industry watching them rewrite history. So, here’s to Cup of Joe: the Baguio boys who turned a ghost story into a global anthem. May their coffee stay strong and their charts keep climbing.

3.content:
**Published** May 1, 2025 10:20am

Locked in the four walls of their house during the lockdown restrictions, Cup of Joe lead vocalist Rapha Ridao and his brother, Red, poured out their emotions and gave birth to the hit song "Multo."

Little did they know that the song will come crashing into the [Billboard Global 200 charts](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942862/cup-of-joe-multo-billboard-global-200/story/) five years later and help catapult the band into a different level of success.

"Kaming dalawa (ng kuya ko) 'yung nagsulat nung pandemic kasi nung time na 'yung 'di kami makalabas, wala kaming ibang (alam) gawin. It gave us time to reflect din kasi there's no escape nung (time) na 'yun eh," Ridao told GMA News in an interview.

Released in 2024, "Multo" has since fetched more than 60 million streams on Spotify. It's become so popular on TikTok, and has been used as an unofficial love song for popular [PBB love team](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942027/cup-of-joe-gian-bernardino-will-ashley-bianca-de-vera/story/) Will Ashley and Bianca de Vera.

With listeners having different interpretations and entries to the viral hit, Cup of Joe discussed the meaning behind the song and how important it is to them to raise the flag of OPM after the song's success.

**Shadows of the Past**

In 2020, Rapha was feeling a lot of things with the pandemic and felt like something was holding him back.

"Naumpisahan namin 'yung song with the thought of some feeling, some people feel things na kahit ano'ng gawin mo, kahit pilit mong nilalayo, sumusunod sa'yo," he recalled.

With the idea of someone following a person, the singer thought of a ghost or "multo" in Filipino and worked on the song with the said word.

"Napunta sa 'min 'yung thought na what if we use 'yung 'multo' as a figure na sinusundan ka. 'Yung feeling na 'yun, 'yung medyo scary," he said.

For Rapha, he wanted the listeners to feel how it's like to be haunted by your unexplainable thoughts and the past like a ghost.

"Gusto naming mapadama sa kanila 'yung element of being haunted. 'Yung feeling na parang wala ka namang nakikita pero andun pa rin eh, andun 'yung bigat. 'Yung mga emotions that can't be explained naturally 'yung mga ganoon," he said.

With the idea of making their album, "Multo" also helped Cup of Joe to circle around the five stages of grief with their album "Silakbo" released in January.

While the song quickly gained traction, processing its success was slow and enduring.

“Actually na-feel lang namin nung time na nagpahinga kami, nag-break from gigs tas doon namin nakikita na ‘ito na pala ‘yun’ ‘yung song na ‘to, No. 1 na,” said Gab Fernandez.

“Hindi namin siya ma-feel nang maayos kasi hindi kami magkakasama pero parang nung nagkasama-sama na kami parang doon lang namin na-feel ‘yung success namin,” he added.

Lead vocalist Gian Bernardino was glad with the reception of the song stressing how the varying interpretations of people with the song are valid.

"It goes along with the other songs na ni-release namin. We created the song with an initial thought then we shared it with the world then they came off with a different perspective and interpretation of the song," the singer said.

"Dahil doon marami rin kaming natututunang perspective which inspires us, which motivates us. Kung ano man 'yung interpretation niyo ng 'Multo,' it's all valid," he added.

**Long Overdue**

Recently reaching 10 million monthly listeners on Spotify — the most for a Filipino act — Cup of Joe stands among the likes of equally successful OPM acts like Juan Karlos, BINI, and Earl Agustin. Gian is just proud to be in the elite cadre.

“Nakaka-proud, we're very thankful na part kami ng generation ng OPM na talagang nare-recognize internationally,” he said.

Keyboardist Xen Gareza is quick to point to social media in helping them reach a wider audience, saying "'yung generation natin, we have the platform to reach international audiences so that's a big help and I believe na even then 'yung talent ng OPM talagang meron na."

“It's only now that we have the platform to go global or to reach further audiences na nare-recognize na rin nila 'yung skills ng Filipinos making art, music,” he added.

Gian stressed how it’s “long overdue” for more OPM acts to gain recognition internationally and it’s time for more artists to join them.

“Actually, long overdue na eh. OPM is very beautiful. It's very unique. It's something na could make waves internationally and I think it's time na rin kasi dati pa talaga dapat 'to. We're glad na we're part of that movement or mechanism na nag-start ng pagkilala ng mundo sa OPM,” he said.

Rafa and CJ Fernandez thanked their supporters and stressed how they made their success possible.

“Thank you kasi ever since 'yung support niyo ramdam na ramdam namin dito (sa puso) ... We're gonna make you guys happy and show you the love na pinapakita niyo sa amin,” Rafa said.

“Sobrang excited namin sa mga following months pa para sa lahat ng mangyayari kaya ayun sana abangan niyo,” CJ added.

Right now, Gian said that they are in the works of introducing more of the other songs in the “Silakbo” album to their listeners noting how there’s more to show with the tracks.

“Gusto lang namin sabihin, you're gonna like this, you've been waiting for this pero in terms of our music, we still have the whole year to introduce the whole album to, not only the Philippines but to the whole world, kasi there's more to see, to hear, to know about the 'Silakbo' album,” he said.

That, and relishing the moment's success.

"As a band we're very much immersing ourselves at the moment, kumbaga, we're living the moment. We're not really pressuring ourselves to achieve greater heights at where we are right now,” the lead vocalist said.

“As much as possible, we do our best every time and bonus na lang kung ano 'yung magiging reception ng tao,” he added. **— LA, GMA Integrated News**

Cup of Joe’s ‘Multo’ Proves a Sad Banger Can Still Be a Breakthrough
====================================================================

The Baguio boyband known for bops embraces heartbreak, and ‘Multo’ quietly rewrites their legacy.

By [Elijah Pareño](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/author/elijah-pareno/ "Posts by Elijah Pareño") April 11, 2025

[![Image 13: Facebook](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/wp-content/themes/rollingstone-philippines/addtoany/icons/facebook.svg)](https://www.addtoany.com/add_to/facebook?linkurl=https%3A%2F%2Frollingstonephilippines.com%2Fmusic%2Fcup-of-joes-multo-proves-a-sad-banger-can-still-be-a-breakthrough%2F&linkname=Cup%20of%20Joe%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Multo%E2%80%99%20Proves%20a%20Sad%20Banger%20Can%20Still%20Be%20a%20Breakthrough "Facebook")[![Image 14: Twitter](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/wp-content/themes/rollingstone-philippines/addtoany/icons/twitter.svg)](https://www.addtoany.com/add_to/twitter?linkurl=https%3A%2F%2Frollingstonephilippines.com%2Fmusic%2Fcup-of-joes-multo-proves-a-sad-banger-can-still-be-a-breakthrough%2F&linkname=Cup%20of%20Joe%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Multo%E2%80%99%20Proves%20a%20Sad%20Banger%20Can%20Still%20Be%20a%20Breakthrough "Twitter")[![Image 15: Email](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/wp-content/themes/rollingstone-philippines/addtoany/icons/email.svg)](https://www.addtoany.com/add_to/email?linkurl=https%3A%2F%2Frollingstonephilippines.com%2Fmusic%2Fcup-of-joes-multo-proves-a-sad-banger-can-still-be-a-breakthrough%2F&linkname=Cup%20of%20Joe%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Multo%E2%80%99%20Proves%20a%20Sad%20Banger%20Can%20Still%20Be%20a%20Breakthrough "Email")[![Image 16: Copy Link](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/wp-content/themes/rollingstone-philippines/addtoany/icons/link.svg)](https://www.addtoany.com/add_to/copy_link?linkurl=https%3A%2F%2Frollingstonephilippines.com%2Fmusic%2Fcup-of-joes-multo-proves-a-sad-banger-can-still-be-a-breakthrough%2F&linkname=Cup%20of%20Joe%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Multo%E2%80%99%20Proves%20a%20Sad%20Banger%20Can%20Still%20Be%20a%20Breakthrough "Copy Link")

    ![Image 17: Cup of Joe](https://b3745597.smushcdn.com/3745597/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/RSPH-Landscape-66-e1744375269471.jpg?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

“Multo” now has 2.55 million daily streamPhoto from Cup of Joe/Facebook

The synth-pop ballad “Multo” by Cup of Joe shouldn’t have worked for the Baguio-based band. Known for their charismatic stage performance and the dual vocals of Gian Bernardino and Raphael Ridao, the group built their name on upbeat pop that’s bred from the pine trees of Baguio City. Yet when they released the melancholic track last October, months before the official release of their debut album _Silakbo_, it revealed an emotional depth fans hadn’t anticipated.

Initially overlooked, “Multo” has since become a slow-burning phenomenon, joining other surprise hits like [Hev Abi’](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/tag/hev-abi/ "Hev Abi")s “Alam Mo Ba Girl” and Maki’s “Dilaw” in dominating charts long after release. But for Cup of Joe, it was an artistic awakening. The lyrics “Pasindi na ng ilaw/ Minumulto na ‘ko ng damdamin ko” resonate as a metaphor for the band’s own evolution, shedding their playful image to confront the ghosts of their musical journey. To add to the virality, some listeners have reinterpreted its ghostly imagery through deeply personal lenses: [TikTok](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/tag/tiktok/ "TikTok") users attribute it to lost loved ones, faded friendships, or even the specter of past selves. “Multo got me on a chokehold beh,” one comment reads, “feeling ko meron akong ex of 7 years.”

![Image 18: Cup of Joe](https://b3745597.smushcdn.com/3745597/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Untitled-design-21.webp?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

_Silakbo_ revealed an emotional depth fans hadn’t anticipated. Photo from Cup of Joe/Facebook

Their stripped-down Cozy Cove performance, now amassing 3.3 million views as of this writing, showcased this transformation in the live footage. Gone were the theatrics; in their place stood raw vulnerability, with haunting lighting underscoring the song’s emotional weight. Even their sold-out two-night concert felt like vindication, proving their artistry extended beyond spectacle.

Advertisement

What makes “Multo” remarkable is its timing. Arriving after the initial hype of _Silakbo_, it defied the usual post-album slump, growing bigger than the band itself. Like Mayonnaise and [Kitchie Nadal](https://rollingstonephilippines.com/tag/kitchie-nadal/ "Kitchie Nadal")’s career resurgences, it reveals an essential truth: the most enduring art often simmers before it boils over, lingering like the ghost it’s named after, long after trends fade.

For a band once defined by youthful exuberance, “Multo” marks Cup of Joe’s arrival as serious pop storytellers. The numbers prove it, but the real victory lies in how a song about the past has become the foundation for their future.

**Editor’s Note:** This article was edited on October 29, 2025, to correct information regarding Cup of Joe’s origins as a boy band. They were, in fact, never a boy band due to the lack of stylized choreography in their repertoire.

PHOTOS: Viva Records

Cup of Joe recently released their official music video for "Multo," a single from their latest album "Silakbo," which features compelling performances by actors Miles Ocampo and Elijah Canlas.

[Cup of Joe](https://www.pikapika.ph/pikadaily/silakbo-new-album-and-soldout-2-day-concert-show-growth-of-cup-of-joe), the acclaimed Filipino pop band, has unveiled the [official music video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CcS1fsuT10M) for their latest single "Multo" featuring notable performances by actors [Miles Ocampo](https://www.pikapika.ph/pikadaily/miles-ocampo-reveals-she-and-ex-elijah-canlas-are-attempting-to-rekindle-relationship/local-news-1) and [Elijah Canlas](https://www.pikapika.ph/pikadaily/elijah-canlas-to-his-late-brother-jm-i-miss-you-more-than-words/local-news-1). This release marks a significant milestone in the band’s musical journey, offering fans a visual and auditory treat that delves into themes of love, loss, and longing.

“Multo,” a track from Cup of Joe's recently released album Silakbo, explores the haunting memories of past relationships and the lingering emotions that accompany them. The music video artfully portrays this narrative, with the beautiful direction of Kris Cazin, adding Miles and Elijah’s compelling performances that encapsulate the song's emotional depth. The real-life couple’s on-screen chemistry brings the song's poignant lyrics to life, offering viewers a relatable and heartfelt experience.

Miles Ocampo, known for her versatile acting skills and previous roles in Philippine television dramas, brings a nuanced portrayal of a woman grappling with the ghosts of her past. Elijah Canlas, acclaimed for his award-winning performances in films and series, complements Ocampo’s role, adding layers of complexity to the storyline. Their collaboration in the "Multo" music video showcases their acting prowess and adds a cinematic quality to the band's musical narrative.

Silakbo, the album featuring “Multo,” is Cup of Joe's latest offering, released on January 17, 2025. The album, which translates to "outburst" or "explosion of emotions," takes listeners on an emotional journey through ten meticulously crafted tracks, each reflecting different facets of human experiences and emotions. From upbeat melodies to soulful ballads, Silakbo showcases the band's versatility and growth, solidifying their place in the contemporary Filipino music scene.

In support of the album, Cup of Joe has announced their "Silakbo" concert tour, set to kick off this 2025. The tour promises to bring the band's new music to fans across the Philippines, specifically in the cities of Davao and Cebu, offering live performances that capture the essence of their latest work. Tickets are now available, and fans are encouraged to secure their spots for an unforgettable musical experience.

The "Multo” music video is now streaming on various platforms, including YouTube and Apple Music. Fans can also listen to the full Silakbo album on major music streaming services. With this release, Cup of Joe continues to captivate audiences with their heartfelt music and storytelling prowess, further establishing their footprint in the music industry.

Cup of Joe is once again proving its star power, sweeping major music accolades in the Philippines.

The “Multo” hitmakers have officially been crowned Billboard Philippines’ No. 1 Artist of 2025, adding yet another milestone to their already remarkable run.

The Top Artists of 2025 party, held on December 3 at Nokal Manila, gathered some of the country’s biggest and brightest talents. The event highlighted the diversity and creative range of OPM, showcasing genres and styles that continue to resonate with a wide spectrum of Filipino music fans.

The Baguio-based band dominated the Billboard Philippines Hot 100, sitting at the top spot for 27 consecutive weeks with their viral single “Multo.” This achievement cements the track as the longest-running No. 1 song in the chart’s history.

However, their winning streak didn’t stop there. Cup of Joe also took home two major awards at the Filipino Music Awards last October, Album of the Year for "Silakbo" and [Song of the Year](https://dzrh.com.ph/post/an-anthem-remembered-cup-of-joes-multo-wins-song-of-the-year-at-filipino-music-awards) for “Multo,” further proving their impact on today’s OPM scene.

The band also created history as the first Filipino act to enter the Billboard Global 200, marking a significant step not only for their career but also for the global recognition of OPM.

Their consistent wins are opening new opportunities, elevating the group to international recognition while pushing Filipino music onto the global stage.

13.title: SG93ICdNdWx0bycgYnkgQ3VwIG9mIEpvZSByZXN1cmZhY2VzIHRoZSBncmllZiBJIG5ldmVyIHJlY292ZXJlZCBmcm9t
13.content:
Cup of Joe’s ‘Multo’ has taken the Philippines by storm, and listeners have tied different interpretations to the song. Some view it as an anthem for unfinished business. Some, for death. It can also be about how the dreams you once chased ended up being the ones chasing you. There are multiple explanations, all made by various people who experienced the same thing–loss.

_Ang malalim na balon ng kahulugan ay nabuksan para sa Multo.. At para sa’kin, nando’n ka sa pinakailalim._

(I guess love really does make its way into the deepest, darkest crannies of a person.)

These days, they don’t ask about you anymore. I guess that’s what moving on looks like to everyone else: less talk, fewer breakdowns, and more smiles in public. Inaasar pa nga ako na hindi na ako “missing-in-action” sa mga gala. So, I continue to play my part. I laugh, post happy pictures, and when the situation allows it, I try to flirt back.

But when that song starts to play, I feel the familiar tightness in my throat, that sudden need to blink too fast, too much. I freeze.

I remember.

Because no matter how good I’ve gotten at convincing everyone else, I can’t lie to myself. The lyrics feel like a secret note addressed only to me. I hear _“Dahil sa bawat tingin, mukha mo'y nakikita,”_ and suddenly, I’m back at your apartment, watching you cook and smile at me while I prepare the table. Time warps around me. Everything goes on rewind mode. And it’s not that I intentionally choose to go back. It’s just... I never really left.

People think ghosts are these scary monsters from movies you’ve avoided like a coward. But this is different. There are no flickering lights or gusts of cold winds whenever I remember you. You just show up in scent, in sound, in silence. You haunt my mornings when I wake up late. You’re in the empty side of my bed, in the song that plays while I’m pretending to clean, in the seat I reserve while knowing that you will never even claim it again.

You’re the ghost I welcomed in because letting go felt worse than being haunted.

Among all the interpretations of Cup of Joe’s ‘Multo,’ for me, it is the permission I never gave myself to admit–I’m not over you. And I don’t know if I ever will be.

But maybe, just maybe, I don’t have to fake it forever. Maybe the song’s reminding me that there’s no shame in grieving someone who’s still alive, just no longer yours.

After all, some ghosts linger not to torment us but to remind us of how deeply we loved.

Cup of Joe drops 'Multo' music video starring Elijah Canlas and Miles Ocampo
============================================================================

By GMA Integrated News

**Published** March 7, 2025 11:37am  

Cup of Joe has released the official music video for their song “Multo,” starring Elijah Canlas and Miles Ocampo.

With screenplay written by the band themselves, the music video follows Miles, who experiences hallucinations of her partner, Elijah. They are shown having happy moments in the house they shared, but the scenes then cut to Miles being alone, while Elijah is presumably a ghost.

“Multo” is part of Cup of Joe’s debut album “[Silakbo](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/933185/cup-of-joe-drops-debut-album-silakbo/story/),” released in January.

Cup of Joe is a pop-rock band from Baguio. Formed in 2018, the band’s lineup consists of lead vocalists Gian Bernardino and Raphael Ridao, lead guitarist Gabriel Fernandez, rhythm guitarist CJ Fernandez, keyboardist Xen Gareza, and drummer Elian Akia.

In 2024, they released the music video for “[Misteryoso](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/915782/cup-of-joe-drops-misteryoso-mv-starring-bini-s-jhoanna-and-directed-by-sb19-s-justin/story/),” starring BINI’s Jhoanna and directed by SB19’s Justin.

The band is best known for their songs “Mananatili,” “Tingin” featuring Janine Tenoso, “Estranghero,” “Sinderela,” and “Tataya.”

Meanwhile, Miles and Elijah [confirmed their relationship](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/familyandrelationships/867556/elijah-canlas-on-keeping-relationship-with-miles-ocampo-private-we-just-choose-what-to-s/story/) in May 2022 and [broke up in 2023](https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/showbiznews/relationship/19081/miles-ocampo-at-elijah-canlas-kumpirmadong-hiwalay-na/photo/258078/my-camille).

However, the two are rumored to have [rekindled their romance](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/familyandrelationships/930693/are-elijah-canlas-and-miles-ocampo-back-together/story/) as they were spotted at various events like dinner in Judy Ann Santos’ restaurant, and Jose Manalo and Gene Maranan’s beach wedding. **—Nika Roque/JCB, GMA Integrated News**

==================================================== [P-Pop](https://popjournalofficial.com/category/music/p-pop/) [Paula De La Cruz](https://popjournalofficial.com/author/satuearthmix/)[Aug 12, 2025Sep 1, 2025](https://popjournalofficial.com/music/p-pop/cup-of-joe-multo-breaks-another-record/) ![Image 3: cup of joe spotify](https://i0.wp.com/popjournalofficial.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Cup-of-Joe-1.jpg?resize=1440%2C1080&ssl=1) “Multo” by Cup of Joe breaks the record for the longest-running #1 song on the Spotify Philippines Daily Chart! --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- **“Multo”** by **Cup of Joe** breaks the record for the longest-running #1 song on the Spotify Philippines Daily Chart, which is currently held by Zack Tabudlo’s “Pano.” They are now getting closer to OPM immortality in a storyline twist that could make for a teleserye cliffhanger. This moment not only commemorates Cup of Joe’s explosive rise but also marks in an exciting new era for OPM. ![Image 4: cup of joe spotify](https://i0.wp.com/popjournalofficial.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/IMG_5577.jpg?resize=819%2C1024&ssl=1) **You Might Also Like: [5 Underrated Cup of Joe Songs if You Liked Multo](https://popjournalofficial.com/news/featured/5-underrated-cup-of-joe-songs-multo/)** ### “Multo” by Cup of Joe Achievements With over 1.18 million daily streams since its debut, “Multo” has become a streaming sensation. It has been the top-ranked song for an incredible 210 days and the number-one song for 125 days (and counting!). It even broke records for the most plays in a single day in Spotify PH history at the same time. The song reached an unsettlingly high 2.3 million plays in a single day. If that’s not hauntingly impressive, we don’t know what is. However, “Multo” went beyond local dominance. OPM is no longer simply a local love affair, as seen by the song’s ghostly high at #80 and its status as the first Filipino act to make it onto the Billboard Global 200. Back home, the song had the longest run in the history of the Billboard Philippines Hot 100, dominating the chart for ten weeks in a row. Cup of Joe’s star power is very much alive, so there’s no need for a séance. Their distinct blend of soul, synth, and heartbreaking sincerity resonates deeply with a generation that is all too familiar with heartbreak. Like its title suggests, “Multo” exists in both your Spotify playlist and the hearts of Joewahs everywhere, floating between realms. [Cup of Joe](https://x.com/cupofjoemusic) is far from done, and the record is still very much in sight. The Smart Araneta Coliseum will host their upcoming three-day SOLD OUT concert, _Stardust._ The band is fired up and ready to create waves once more. Fans, also known as the devoted Joewahs, are anticipated to turn up, sing loudly, and cry harder. OPM is alive, thriving, and poised to haunt not only our hearts but also the world stage, if “Multo” has taught us anything. **Also Read: [Cup of Joe is Back with Third Major Solo Concert, Stardust](https://popjournalofficial.com/events/cup-of-joe-third-major-solo-concert-stardust/)** * * * Press Release [![Image 5](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/96f0be797e5c2984fc0353f5e9d470aa382dc2426f5c5fd8768d5a286956d016?s=150&d=mm&r=g)](https://popjournalofficial.com/author/satuearthmix/) #### [Paula De La Cruz](https://popjournalofficial.com/author/satuearthmix/) Aside from being a student, Paula enjoys many things: boys’ love series, k-dramas, k-pop, manhwas, anime, and anything related to music. Cup of Joe is Billboard Philippines' no. 1 artist of 2025
=========================================================

By GMA Integrated News

**Published** December 4, 2025 9:32am  

![Image 9: Cup of Joe is Billboard Philippines' no. 1 artist of 2025](https://images.gmanews.tv/webpics/2025/04/multo_2025_04_15_18_50_23.jpg)

Photo: Cup of Joe/IG

Billboard Philippines has crowned Cup of Joe as its no. 1 artist of 2025!

The magazine said that the OPM band claimed the year as theirs, "exploding in popularity" the past year.

Cup of Joe topped the Billboard Philippines Hot 100 for 27 straight weeks with their viral hit, "Multo."

The five-member band was also the most streamed OPM artist on Spotify Philippines in 2025, while "Multo" was the most streamed song.

Other Stories
-------------

[### 'Multo' is most streamed song on Spotify PH in 2025; Cup of Joe is most streamed OPM artist](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/968432/multo-is-most-streamed-song-on-spotify-ph-in-2025-cup-of-joe-is-most-streamed-opm-artist/story/ "'Multo' is most streamed song on Spotify PH in 2025; Cup of Joe is most streamed OPM artist")

[### Cup of Joe, BINI, Ely Buendia, and more to perform at Wonderful Moments Music Festival](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/963422/cup-of-joe-bini-ely-buendia-and-more-to-perform-at-wonderful-moments-music-festival/story/ "Cup of Joe, BINI, Ely Buendia, and more to perform at Wonderful Moments Music Festival")

[### SB19 dominates first-ever Filipino Music Awards; Cup of Joe bags song, album of the year](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/artandculture/963263/sb19-dominates-first-ever-filipino-music-awards-cup-of-joe-bags-song-album-of-the-year/story/ "SB19 dominates first-ever Filipino Music Awards; Cup of Joe bags song, album of the year")

Here's the full list of Billboard Philippines' Top Artists of 2025:

1.  Cup of Joe
2.  Dionela
3.  Arthur Nery
4.  Shanti Dope
5.  December Avenue
6.  TJ Monterde
7.  Ben&Ben
8.  Earl Agustin
9.  Hellmerry
10.  Maki

Billboard Philippines called 2025 a "momentous time for Filipino music."

"Whether it has been measured in chart data or cultural impact, these artists have been taking Filipino craft to another level, one hit at a time," it said about its Top Artists of 2025 list. "Each of his anthems, both old and new, solidifies in the Philippine soundscape as a staple, not only as hits but as a pop culture phenomenon." **—JCB, GMA Integrated News**

Cup of Joe's 'Multo' makes it to Billboard Global 200
=====================================================

By GMA Integrated News

**Published** April 15, 2025 6:51pm  

![Image 9: Cup of Joes's 'Multo' makes it to Billboard Global 200](https://images.gmanews.tv/webpics/2025/04/multo_2025_04_15_18_50_23.jpg)

Photo: Spotify

Cup of Joe's "Multo" is making waves on international charts!

The hit song from the OPM band has made it to the Billboard Global 200 this week at no. 181, ahead of "Handlebars" by Jennie and Dua Lipa (no. 186) and "Toxic Til The End" by Rosé (no. 194).

"Multo" is a mapanakit song about the yearning for a lost love. The song has been popular on TikTok and was recently used in edits of WillCa, the "[Pinoy Big Brother](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/942690/pinoy-big-brother-celebrity-collab-edition-here-is-the-complete-roster-of-housemates/story/)" love team between [Will Ashley](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/942683/will-ashley-nation-s-son/story/) and [Bianca De Vera](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/942483/bianca-de-vera-opens-up-to-river-joseph-about-will-ashley-i-ll-always-care-about-him/story/).

Cup of Joe's vocalist, [Gian Bernardino](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942027/cup-of-joe-gian-bernardino-will-ashley-bianca-de-vera/story/), admitted to feeling kilig over the WillCa videos.

The song was released as a single last year. It has since fetched over 60 million streams on Spotify. It was also included in Cup of Joe's debut album "[Silakbo](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/933185/cup-of-joe-drops-debut-album-silakbo/story/)," which dropped in January.

"Multo" has a music video starring [Elijah Canlas and Miles Ocampo](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/938503/cup-of-joe-drops-multo-music-video-starring-elijah-canlas-and-miles-ocampo/story/).

Cup of Joe's other songs include "Misteryoso," "Tingin," "Estranghero," and "Ikaw Pa Rin Ang Piliin Ko." **—MGP, GMA Integrated News**

2](https://assets.myx.global/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/L1GROUP-107-2-683x1024.jpg) The only ‘ghosting’ we want: Cup of Joe’s “Multo” haunts Spotify PH all the way to No. 1 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Posted By: MYX Global Post Date: August 18, 2025 In a plot twist worthy of a teleserye cliffhanger, **Cup of Joe**’s runaway hit **“Multo”** is creeping closer and closer to OPM immortality. The beloved five-piece band is on the brink of making OPM history, as **“Multo”** breaks the record for the **longest-running #1 song on the Spotify Philippines Daily Chart** – a title currently held by Zack Tabudlo’s “Pano.” It’s a moment that not only celebrates Cup of Joe’s meteoric rise but also marks an exciting new chapter for OPM. Since its release, “Multo” has become a full-blown streaming phenomenon, racking up **over 1.18 million streams a day** and holding the highest spot for a jaw-dropping **210 days and the #1 spot for 125 days** (and counting!). At one point, it even shattered records for the **highest single-day streams in Spotify PH history**, clocking in at a spooky-good **2.3 million** plays in just 24 hours. If that’s not hauntingly impressive, we don’t know what is. But “Multo” didn’t stop at just local domination. The song also made global waves, becoming the **first Filipino act to enter the Billboard Global 200**, eventually peaking at **#80**, a ghostly milestone that proves OPM is no longer just a local love affair. Back home, the track ruled the **Billboard Philippines Hot 100 for 10 straight weeks**, the longest run in the chart’s history. No need for a séance, Cup of Joe’s star power is very much alive. Their unique fusion of soul, synth, and aching sincerity strikes a deep chord with a generation all too familiar with heartbreak. “Multo” floats between worlds, just like its title – existing both in your Spotify loop and in the hearts of Joewahs everywhere. With the record well within reach, **Cup of Joe is far from finished**. The band is fired up and ready to make waves once again with their upcoming **3-day SOLD OUT Concert titled ‘Stardust’ at the Smart Araneta Coliseum** where fans (aka the ever-dedicated **Joewahs**) are expected to show up, sing loud, and cry harder. Because if “Multo” has taught us anything, it’s that OPM is alive, thriving, and ready to haunt not just our hearts, but also the global stage. Spread the word. of Joe- Silakbo (Album Review) ================================== By Christy At September 03, 2025 0 [![Image 2](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiZfNVDdaSdjLvsuFgEQcsMY9nu4KioWo-EA937AUiOVAUYhSMu8zvXfh0TeRe72WFt044xvbYKeMQiiC5gkcG8i2IDoxmYf2ih9JHY_LCvTOmvcTaqgmU46cBkYDKymNyKuH0IMEgREAXD6uzuaCTC4kIzboTJFuDozE3KTk3SmVqQqfKIhiv5nsP2A14/s16000-rw/Screenshot%202025-08-15%20at%205.38.24%E2%80%AFPM.png)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiZfNVDdaSdjLvsuFgEQcsMY9nu4KioWo-EA937AUiOVAUYhSMu8zvXfh0TeRe72WFt044xvbYKeMQiiC5gkcG8i2IDoxmYf2ih9JHY_LCvTOmvcTaqgmU46cBkYDKymNyKuH0IMEgREAXD6uzuaCTC4kIzboTJFuDozE3KTk3SmVqQqfKIhiv5nsP2A14/s1268/Screenshot%202025-08-15%20at%205.38.24%E2%80%AFPM.png)If there’s an album that can accompany us through the stormiest and darkest of days, it has to be rising Pinoy experimental pop band [Cup of Joe’s](https://www.facebook.com/CupOfJoeRecords/) seminal full-length release, _Silakbo_. Dropped on January 17, 2025, the album’s Filipino title translates to “emotional outburst” or “roused-up feelings.” Its black-and-red cover art symbolically represents the five stages of grief—or alternately, the five talented Gen Z members that make up the band. Frontmen **Gian Bernardino** and **Rapha Ridao** provide soulful, contrasting-yet-blending vocals, while **Gabriel Fernandez** (lead guitar), **CJ Fernandez** (rhythm guitar), and **Xen Gareza** (keyboards) craft a sonically layered soundscape drawing from retro, indie, folk, and pop ballad influences. Cup of Joe’s strength lies in their romantic Tagalog lyricism and dreamy imagery, a powerful medium for connecting to their growing legion of fans. Listeners will find themselves immersed in the album’s expressive sensibilities and its heartfelt confrontation with grief’s thematic cousins—denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance. Prepare to have dormant feelings resurface at your most vulnerable moments, as Cup of Joe invites you to sit once again with emotions that may never have found closure. ****DENIAL: “Bagyo” and “Wine”**** The opener _Bagyo_ begins with the swirling sound of an impending thunderstorm, mirroring the emotional turbulence of circumstances beyond one’s control. Its metaphor of a falling sky and rising tide of misfortune highlights the inevitability of pain. No matter how hard we resist, the rain still falls, and the world still turns dark. Meanwhile, _Wine_—the only track with an English title and chorus—delivers disbelief and disappointment at losing a lover to someone else. Minimal instrumentation and Ridao’s warm, sensual vocals make this haunting ballad unforgettable. ### **ANGER: “Kanelang Mata” and “Bubog”** _Kanelang Mata_ (Cinnamon Eyes) simmers slowly before escalating into a full storm of anger. _Bubog_ (Shards), however, cuts deepest—it’s raw, nerve-hitting, and emotionally devastating, driven by self-doubt, inadequacy, and self-blame. Bernardino and Ridao deliver lines with such piercing emotion that listeners are left asking: _Is the mirror broken, or am I the one who’s broken?_ From a songwriting perspective, _Bubog_ is easily a standout. ### **BARGAINING: “Siping” and “Pahina”** Grief shifts into longing in this section. _Siping_ (To Lay Beside) flows like a serenade—a final warm embrace before letting go. _Pahina_ (Page), meanwhile, aches with the desire to rewrite life’s chapters and cling to promises etched in memory. Its lyrical strength lies in its poetic imagery, repeating the inevitability of returning to the same person, the same page. ### **DEPRESSION: “Multo” and “’Di Maari”** Despite its heavy theme, _Multo_ is the most popular and heavily rotated song on the album—thanks to its catchy riffs and relatable lyrics about missed connections, lost chances, and unfulfilled dreams. It’s poised to cement Cup of Joe as a household OPM name. _’Di Maari_, on the other hand, is a stripped-down gem. With bare-bones instrumentation and lyrics that feel like a whispered love letter or apology, it is deeply healing in its intimacy. ### **ACCEPTANCE: “Hinga” and “Silakbo”** The final stage of grief comes with renewed energy and hope. _Hinga_ provides a collective pause to breathe, lifted by exhilarating drum beats and soaring falsettos. Its message is clear: even darkness allows stars to shine. Finally, the eponymous track _Silakbo_ closes the album on a high. Upbeat, danceable, and vocally dynamic, it encapsulates the band’s versatility and emotional journey. Even if sung a cappella, the power of these songs would remain undeniable. ### **Final Verdict** _Silakbo_ is a musically mature release overflowing with lyrical depth and emotional resonance. Each of its ten tracks stands out in its own style while contributing to a cohesive narrative arc. It’s a beautiful balance of pain, reflection, and catharsis—an album that speaks to both new and long-time OPM listeners. [](https://interaksyon.philstar.com/celebrities/2025/03/07/292969/miles-ocampo-elijah-canlas-star-in-cup-of-joes-multo-music-video/#)

Former celebrity couple **Miles Ocampo** and **Elijah Canlas,** who are rumored to be back together, starred in the music video for **Cup of Joe’s** single, “Multo,” released on Thursday evening, March 6.

The track is part of the band’s new album, “Silakbo”.

The two actors showcased their acting prowess in the video, earning praise from viewers.

“Ang galing ni Miles magswitch ng emotions from happy to sad” one commented.

“Kudos to Miles and Elijah for doing a great job! Galing! Damang-dama ko yung sakit eh,” another wrote.

Meanwhile, the comment section was filled with Filipinos sharing their thoughts about the song.

“‘Tanging panalangin, lubayan na sana’—but a part of you never wanted it to go away, because it’s the only thing that was ever left in you; ang tanging pinanghahawakan mo, ang tanging natira mula sa nawala,” one longingly said.

“Fully healed sa umaga, ‘bakit pa kasi ako umamin’ sa gabi,” another quipped.

“Memories feel like weapons talaga. One minute, it can be the shield, keeping you protected from the pain you’ve been running away from. The next thing you know, it was the sword that pierced through–reminding you that the shield was only made of your softest fabric–sharp, and was meant to stab you,” a YouTube user commented.

The music video has so far garnered 114,000 views and is the Top 17 trending video for music on YouTube.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://annual.wikimedia.org/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

34% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

11% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities.  Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://annual.wikimedia.org/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

34% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

11% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.
